deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- not runnable by agent: this CRPS-blackbox case must Over current on output (forcing an over-current condition on the PSU output) so the PSU blackbox records it, using fault-injection hardware/throttle/AC on the physical PSU, and then reads the blackbox/fault log - a physical, destructive fault injection a person must perform. Agent cannot inject PSU input/output faults or read the physical blackbox.

original_test_intent: Verify that a controlled output over-current event on a specified PSU rail is persisted in the PSU blackbox with the expected fault status and timeline.
original_method: A qualified operator uses an isolated programmable load/fault fixture to apply the approved rail-specific current profile while independent instrumentation and cutoff protect the DUT. The raw blackbox event is then extracted and correlated with measured current, protection response and recovery.
manual_activity: The operator must configure and supervise the physical load/fault fixture and cutoff. Agent automation may collect measurements and extract/correlate blackbox data only after the complete method is approved.
required_inputs: PSU/DUT identity, target rail and normal load state
Vendor-approved current threshold/waveform, tolerance, duration and expected OCP response
Rated programmable load or fault fixture, wiring limits, calibrated current/voltage capture and cutoff
Blackbox extraction interface/schema and expected over-current record
Qualified operator, inspection/recovery procedure and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Do not use an uncontrolled short, unknown load, register write, protection bypass or AC manipulation to create over-current.
Validate cable/connector/load ratings, isolation, calibration and hard cutoff before energizing.
Preserve baseline logs and protect unrelated/production loads.
Stop on uncontrolled current, voltage collapse, overheating, smoke, arcing, damage, shutdown or management loss.
No automatic reinjection, retry, reset or power cycle.
agent_execution_scope: Validate plan/evidence configuration and collect permitted pre-event state.
After operator stimulus, retain actual current/voltage/time traces and raw blackbox export.
Correlate OCP behavior, event code/fields and recovery timeline.
Report facts without driving the load or deciding the verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve and operate the load/fault fixture and cutoff envelope.
Inspect wiring/PSU/load and restore the safe state.
Provide inaccessible blackbox data and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The refusal is directionally safe, but the statement is not a test method and its throttle/AC alternatives are not equivalent to a measured output-current profile.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the approved programmable-load/fixture SOP and vendor blackbox extraction interface; no generic shell command can define or safely create the event.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Attended Time 5 and Machine Time 5 are retained but do not establish a current amplitude or dwell.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Specify one rail/current/time profile below fixture and wiring limits, synchronize calibrated traces, execute once under operator control, and correlate the immutable blackbox event and protection response.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the named PSU, rail, wiring, load and calibrated fixture approved by engineering.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record PSU/BMC firmware, fixture/load firmware, calibration and blackbox schema/tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project/vendor OCP and blackbox documentation must be supplied; no current threshold or stimulus is invented.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds measurable rail/current/time and cutoff boundaries while preserving the blackbox goal.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One rail/profile verifies only that OCP record path, not all loads, rails or short-circuit behavior.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Rail/current profile, fixture ratings, monitoring/cutoff, expected record and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Connector/wiring heating and energy delivery make even a brief current fault hazardous if limits or topology are wrong.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve a bounded programmable-load method and reduced current/duration if its coverage is recorded. AC removal, a software workload or an unmeasured short cannot be claimed as equivalent over-current injection.
expected_evidence: Approved OCP profile, rail, load/fixture ratings, calibration and safety checklist
Operator record and calibrated current/voltage/time trace with cutoff/protection response
Raw blackbox export with schema/tool version and expected OCP-field comparison
Preserved platform logs plus wiring/PSU/load inspection and recovery evidence

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item identifies the over-current status whose blackbox persistence is checked. Procedure and criterion are consistent but insufficiently parameterized.

blocked_analysis.analysis: No rail, current/time envelope, safe fixture or expected record exists. Guessing any of them is unsafe and changes coverage, so this is a genuine BLOCKED condition.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agree the agent cannot inject the fault; reject speculative physical methods and the unsupported absolute blackbox-access claim.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agree with BLOCKED and its rail/profile/fixture/measurement/recovery requirements.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Defines which evidence could later be automated and distinguishes OCP coverage from AC or generic fault behavior.

review_improvement: This review gives the over-current case a rail-specific measurable contract, identifies wiring/load hazards, and prevents non-equivalent AC or workload substitutions.
independent_technical_reasoning: A physical operator cannot compensate for absent current/time and fixture limits. Those parameters determine both electrical safety and whether the blackbox code is meaningfully exercised; execution therefore remains BLOCKED until supplied.
